transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you lately that brought you here today?

Yeah, um… honestly, I’m here because I feel like I’m just always running hot. Like there’s this motor in me that doesn’t shut off, even when I know I need to settle down or just… take a breath. It’s not like I’m trying to be difficult or wound up all the time, but that’s how it comes out.

And lately it’s been causing problems at the firehouse. I mean, that job already has enough intensity built into it, you know? But I feel like I’m bringing extra intensity even when it’s not needed, and it’s starting to get me in trouble. I can tell people are noticing, and I don’t want it to keep going that way. That’s really what pushed me to come in.
Have you been experiencing sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or panic, maybe like your heart is racing or you can’t catch your breath?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I know what it feels like to have my heart going because of work or because something intense is happening, but that seems kind of expected in those situations.

Like, I don’t really have these sudden out-of-nowhere moments where I’m terrified and can’t breathe or feel like I’m going to die or anything like that. At least, not that I’ve noticed. I get wound up, sure, but I wouldn’t call it panic, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t know that I’d say “hopeless,” no. I mean, I have bad days, obviously, and there are times where I feel frustrated with myself or kind of worn out from always feeling like I’m trying to rein myself in, but I don’t think it’s the same as being depressed, if that’s what you mean.

As far as losing interest… I’m not sure. I still like the things I like, when I can actually sit with them or make time for them. Sometimes I probably don’t enjoy stuff as much because my head is already somewhere else, or I’m restless, or I’m thinking about what I should be doing next, but it’s not like everything feels pointless or flat. I wouldn’t describe it that way.

So… I guess the short answer is no, not really down or hopeless in that sense. More frustrated and wound up than sad.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem, or having trouble controlling your worrying thoughts?

I’m not sure I’d call it worrying, exactly. I mean, I think about things a lot—probably more than I need to sometimes—but it doesn’t feel like I’m sitting there afraid something terrible is going to happen for no reason.

Like, if there’s an actual issue, sure, I’ll chew on it. If something’s going on at work or there’s something I know I need to handle, my mind can kind of stay on it longer than I want. But when you say “worrying a lot even when there isn’t an immediate problem,” I don’t know… that doesn’t feel like the main thing for me.

It’s more like my mind is busy or jumping around, not necessarily stuck on one fear. I don’t usually feel like I can’t control worrying thoughts in the way you’re describing. At least I haven’t noticed that as a big problem.
Do you often feel restless, like you can't relax or need to keep moving, even when you're trying to slow down?

Yeah… yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the things I notice the most, especially at work.

Like, if I’m in a command meeting and everyone’s seated and going through updates or planning stuff, I can do it, but it feels like my body is just… revving too high. Like I’m sitting there trying to look normal, but inside I’m already halfway out of the chair. I’ll be thinking, can I stand up? Can I go walk the bay? Can I check the rigs? Can I just do something besides sit here planted in one spot?

It’s not even always because the meeting is boring, exactly. Sometimes it’s important, and I know I need to pay attention, but physically it feels almost uncomfortable to stay still. Like there’s pressure building up and moving around would take the edge off. I’ll shift around, change positions, lean forward, lean back, mess with whatever’s in my hands if I have something, that kind of thing.

When I’m trying to slow down, that’s when I notice it more. If there’s something to do, I can throw myself into it, but just sitting still and relaxing… yeah, that does not come naturally to me.
Do you find yourself acting impulsively or having trouble waiting your turn in situations, like you feel the need to jump in or take action right away even if it’s not the best time?

Yeah… I do. Waiting my turn is a bigger issue for me than I probably like to admit.

It can be little stuff, too. Like during equipment checks, if there’s a process and I’m supposed to wait for someone else to finish their part before I do mine, I get really edgy. I’ll know, logically, there’s an order to it and I’m not helping by hovering, but I’ll still be standing there shifting around, watching the time, wanting to step in or move it along. Sometimes I catch myself almost jumping ahead, like, “Okay, let’s just do this part now,” even when it’s not really my turn.

Same thing with medical follow-ups or appointments. If I’m waiting around, I start pacing if I can, or checking the clock over and over, or looking at the door like that’s somehow going to make things happen faster. It’s not that I think I’m more important than anyone else. It just feels like sitting there and waiting quietly takes a stupid amount of effort.

Even in line at the store, I can feel myself getting irritated or keyed up. I’ll switch lanes, check how many items people have, look for some faster way through it. And sometimes I do have this urge to jump in or take action right away, even if the smarter thing would be to just hold back for a minute. So, yeah, waiting my turn definitely makes me restless and impatient.

Have you had trouble with focusing or sustaining attention, especially with tasks that require mental effort, or do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat when you need to stay still?

Yeah, the fidgeting part, absolutely. That’s pretty constant for me, especially if I’m sitting in a meeting or anywhere I’m supposed to stay still and just listen.

I’ll realize my leg has been bouncing the whole time, or I’m clicking a pen over and over, or shifting around in the chair like I can’t get comfortable. Sometimes I’m messing with whatever is in front of me—paperclip, pen, my radio strap, whatever’s there—and I don’t even notice I’m doing it until someone looks at me or I suddenly hear the clicking and think, okay, I should probably stop that.

And then I’ll stop for maybe ten seconds, and before I know it, I’m doing something else. Tapping my foot, changing position, leaning forward, sitting back, rubbing my hands together. It’s like my body is looking for something to do even when I’m trying to be still. So yeah, that part is definitely there.
Looking back, did you notice these kinds of feelings—being restless, having trouble waiting, or difficulty staying still—when you were a child, like in school or at home?

Yeah… looking back, I guess it was there pretty early. I don’t remember every detail myself, but my mom definitely does. She’s told me more than once that in grade school I was “always moving,” her words. Like I’d be out of my seat when I wasn’t supposed to be, or I’d blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking, and then I’d get in trouble even if I actually knew the answer.

And homework was a whole thing, too. She says I was bright enough to do it, like it wasn’t that I couldn’t understand the work, but I’d lose the worksheet, forget to bring it home, forget to turn it in, that kind of stuff. I remember getting those notes sent home from teachers, like, “He needs to stay seated,” or “He needs to raise his hand,” or “He’s not completing assignments,” and my mom being frustrated because she knew I wasn’t stupid or trying to fail.

So, yeah, it wasn’t just something that started when I became an adult or got into fire service. It sounds like it’s kind of been there since I was a kid.
Do these feelings of restlessness and difficulty staying still happen in different parts of your life, like at home or in your personal relationships, or is it mostly at work?

It’s definitely not just work. Work maybe makes it more obvious because there are structured times where I’m supposed to stand by or sit still, but it happens at home too, pretty much all the time.

Like on my days off, when I’m with my family, I’ll try to do quiet stuff with them—sit and watch something, play a game, just hang out—and I don’t last very long before I’m up again. I’ll start talking through whatever we’re doing, or I’ll get up to “just check something” in the garage, or I’ll remember some tool I wanted to organize, or I’ll walk around the house looking for something to do. And it’s not always something important. A lot of times it’s just… I feel like I can’t stay planted.

Even if I’m sitting with them and I want to be there, I’ll catch myself getting restless pretty quickly. Like I’ll sit down, then shift around, then stand up, then sit on the arm of the couch, then decide I should go look at something in the garage or move something around. Before I know it, I’ve kind of left the family activity even though I didn’t mean to.

So yeah, it affects home too. It’s not like I clock out and suddenly I’m calm and able to sit quietly. My family sees it plenty.
